The `transform` package: `golang.org/x/text/transform`.

Normalization: `golang.org/x/text/unicode/norm` with `norm.NFC`, `norm.NFD`, `norm.NFKC`, `norm.NFKD`, and `.String()`, `.Bytes()`, `norm.Form`.

A convenient design:

```go
package textconv

func ConvertEncoding(src []byte, from, to encoding.Encoding) ([]byte, error)
func Normalize(s string, form norm.Form) string
```

part.text:
Set up the `textconv` Go module:

- `go.mod` — Go 1.27, depends on `golang.org/x/text v0.42.0`.
- `internal/textcodec/encoding.go` — encoding conversion via `x/text/encoding` + `htmlindex` (`LookupEncoding`, `Decode`, `Encode`, `Convert`); accepts WHATWG names like `windows-1252`, `shift_jis`, `gbk`.
- `internal/textcodec/normalize.go` — Unicode normalization via `x/text/unicode/norm` (`LookupForm`, `Normalize`, `IsNormalized`) for NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD.
- `main.go` — CLI: `-from`, `-to`, `-norm`, `-in`, `-out` (stdin/stdout by default).
- Tests pass, `go vet`/`gofmt` clean.

Usage: `textconv -from windows-1252 -to utf-8 -norm NFC -in x.txt -out y.txt`

I chose the module path `textconv` since no remote was configured; let me know if you want it renamed (e.g. `github.com/you/textconv`).
